title: One release version, one cut: release-qualify checks and reserves the version on the storage remote
goal: release-qualify looked for the tag in the local checkout only. On 2026-11-11 v0.21.62 was qualified twice at once: on Windows from its release-lanes line and on Linux from a distilled candidate; the second could not be published. Before any gate runs, release-qualify now refuses a tag already on the remote, refuses a tree that does not contain an open release line of that version, and reserves the version with a create-only blob refs/claims/release-version/<tag> (renewed by its holder, taken over after four hours, dropped when a gate fails).
validation: On x86_64-pc-windows-msvc: 4 new tests on real Git with a bare remote pass (two cuts race and one wins; renewal; own-only release; stale takeover at exactly four hours; published tag refused; bypassed release line refused and a tree on the line admitted; unreachable remote is an error); release-qualify's 14 tests pass; clippy -p xtask --all-targets -D warnings clean. Not exercised: a real release cut through the repository's pre-push hook, and Linux.
limitations: The reservation covers release-qualify only. release-lanes init does not reserve a version, and local-distill does not check one.
A reservation left by a cut that passed but was never published blocks that version for four hours.
Susi Commercial Apps has its own reservation (refs/release-cuts) and is not changed here.
